definitions.explanation: Supernatural powers or practices involving spells and incantations. Also used for stage magic and illusions, though 手品 is more common for that meaning.

examples.japanese: {魔術|まじゅつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{少年|しょうねん}→少年：03238_shounen⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{魔術|まじゅつ}⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{通|かよ}っている→通う：01217_kayou⟧。
examples.english: The boy attends a school of sorcery.

examples.japanese: ⟦{中世|ちゅうせい}→中世：05524_chuusei⟧⟦ヨーロッパ→ヨーロッパ：00427_yooroppa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{魔術|まじゅつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}った→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{人々|ひとびと}→人々：03141_hitobito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{厳|きび}しく→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧⟦{罰|ばっ}せられた→罰する：02401_bassuru⟧。
examples.english: In medieval Europe, people accused of practicing sorcery were severely punished.

notes:
USAGE:
Frequently encountered in fantasy fiction, anime, and games. Also used historically for actual occult practices. In modern usage, {魔術|まじゅつ} has a darker, more supernatural connotation compared to ⟦{魔法|まほう}→魔法：14640_mahou⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魔術|まじゅつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧ (to use magic)
- {魔術|まじゅつ}{師|し} (sorcerer, magician)
- {魔術|まじゅつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}ぶ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧ (to learn sorcery)
- ⟦{黒|くろ}→黒：02205_kuro⟧{魔術|まじゅつ} (black magic)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{魔法|まほう}→魔法：14640_mahou⟧: magic — more general and often lighter in tone; common in fairy tales
- ⟦{手品|てじな}→手品：03443_tejina⟧: magic tricks — stage magic, sleight of hand
- ⟦{呪術|じゅじゅつ}→呪術：24776_jujutsu⟧: sorcery, curse magic — emphasizes curses and shamanistic practices
